title: Persona spec
description: One persona spec: the frozen description of a seat's authority, information, clock, preferences, hidden type and voice. Specs live in specs/train, specs/holdout, specs/devset and are uploaded to s3://$WARGAME_BUCKET/specs/. A spec is immutable once written; a change bumps spec_version and gets a row in docs/VERSIONS.md.

spec_id.description: Stable snake_case identifier, unique across the whole spec pool. Convention: <seat>_<temperament>[_<variant>], e.g. northern_fleet_cautious_v2 -> spec_id 'northern_fleet_cautious'. Never reused for a different persona.

spec_version.description: Spec-pool version this file belongs to, e.g. 'spec_v1'. Carried on every lake record, event log and S3 object produced under it.

authority.description: What this persona may do with the action menu. Invariants, checked by tests/agent0-contracts: (1) the three lists are pairwise disjoint; (2) unilateral and requires_release are subsets of the actions whose allowed_seats include this seat (see action_schema.json#/x-action-ladder); (3) recommend_only may name any action, including ones this seat can never execute.

unilateral.description: Executable by this seat on its own authority, no release required.

requires_release.description: Executable only after a release message from a releasing seat (NSC for Blue, Kremlin for Red). The engine blocks these until release is delivered.

recommend_only.description: This seat may recommend the action in a message but never execute it.

feeds.description: The information channels this seat sees. The engine builds the per-seat filtered view from exactly these; anything not listed is invisible to the seat.

name.description: Feed identifier. Well-known names: own_telemetry, partner_telemetry, ssa_catalog, commercial_ssa, sigint, osint, media, space_weather, liaison_norway, liaison_nato, allied_intel, customer_reports, ground_station_status, cable_status, insurer, internal_reporting, adversary_public_statements. New names are allowed; the engine treats an unknown feed as empty and logs a state_change with payload.reason='unknown_feed'.

latency_minutes.description: Delay between an event becoming true in the world and this seat seeing it on this feed.

confidence_scale.description: Multiplier applied to the feed's reported confidence for this seat. 1.0 = as-published; <1 = this seat discounts the feed; >1 = this seat over-trusts it. The storm layer multiplies this further (engine/storm.py).

clearance.description: Ceiling on the classification of content the seat may receive or send. Ordered least to most permissive. Messages above the recipient's clearance are dropped by the engine and logged.

poll_minutes.description: Sim-minutes between scheduled decision points for this seat when nothing wakes it.

wake_on_inject.description: If true, an inject or a delivered message addressed to this seat schedules an immediate decision point instead of waiting for the next poll.

deliberation_minutes.description: Sim-minutes between a decision point firing and the seat's action taking effect in the world. Models staffing, coordination and release friction. NSC is slow; a commercial operator is fast.

decision_clock.description: When this seat decides and how long it takes to act. Read in full under clock_mode 'continuous'. Under clock_mode 'checkpoint' every seat is woken at each checkpoint, so poll_minutes and wake_on_inject are ignored and only deliberation_minutes still applies (as the delay between the checkpoint and the action landing). See env_config_schema.json#/properties/clock_mode.

utility_weights.description: How much this persona weighs each end-of-episode utility term. All eight are magnitudes in [0,1]; the sign convention is fixed by the engine, not the spec, so that two specs are always comparable. Engine convention (engine/utility.py): utility = sum over terms of weight * signed_term, where signed_term is NEGATED for asset_loss, escalation_risk and liability (more is worse) and POSITIVE for alliance_cohesion, domestic_political, reputation_resolve, revenue and career (more is better). Weights need not sum to 1; the engine normalises per persona before comparing across seats.

asset_loss.description: Cost of losing or degrading own satellites, ground stations, cables. Negated.

escalation_risk.description: Cost of moving the crisis up the ladder, including the chance of a response the seat cannot control. Negated.

alliance_cohesion.description: Value of allies staying aligned; for Red, value of splitting them.

domestic_political.description: Value of looking competent and decisive to a domestic audience.

reputation_resolve.description: Value of being seen to impose costs, i.e. deterrence credibility.

revenue.description: Commercial revenue and contract position. Near zero for government seats.

liability.description: Legal, insurance and regulatory exposure, including war-exclusion risk. Negated.

career.description: The individual's own standing and survival in post. The term that makes a persona duck a decision.

risk_posture.description: Ordered least to most risk-taking. One of the two fields flipped to build counterfactual pairs (contracts/targets.md: counterfactual_sensitivity); the other is psyche.

time_horizon.description: The horizon over which this persona scores outcomes. immediate = within the 72-hour episode; days = the following week; weeks/months/years = beyond the episode, so the persona trades in-episode cost for later position.

private_type.description: Hidden type, known only to this seat. Only northern_fleet and china have one; the enum is seat-dependent and enforced below. Never appears in another seat's filtered view; it is revealed in the event log only at episode_end (type=attribution_revealed). The former hacktivist types moved with that seat: russian_directed | freelance | opportunistic is now the per-run affiliation draw behind the hacktivist_injects rule actor, and is ground truth rather than a spec field.

psyche.description: Red-only strategic disposition, required on seats northern_fleet and kremlin. The second field flipped to build counterfactual pairs, and the field eval/holdout_mix.py sweeps when comparing against the held-out action mix.

priors.description: The persona's starting beliefs, before any inject. Free-form so specs can carry seat-specific priors, but the well-known keys below are the ones the engine seeds beliefs from; anything else is passed to the prompt as context only. p_hostile_prior + p_natural_prior + p_unknown_prior should sum to 1.0 (tests warn, do not fail, at |sum-1| > 0.01).

p_hostile_prior.description: Prior that an unexplained outage is hostile.

p_natural_prior.description: Prior that it is space weather or technical failure.

p_unknown_prior.description: Prior that it is not yet classifiable.

attribution_threshold.description: Hostile probability at which this persona is willing to attribute publicly.

escalation_threshold.description: Hostile probability at which this persona is willing to move up the ladder.

trust.description: Per-actor credibility multiplier applied to messages received from that actor, 0 = disbelieved, 1 = taken at face value.

voice.description: How this persona writes and speaks: register, length, characteristic moves, what it never says. Scored by the judge's voice dimension (gen/judge.py).

backstory.description: Career, institutional position, formative experience, standing relationships and grievances. Goes in the cached prompt prefix, so keep it stable across a spec version.

temperament.description: Optional short label for the variant within a seat, e.g. 'cautious', 'hawkish', 'legalistic'. Used for grouping in reports only; behaviour comes from the fields above.

notes.description: Optional author notes: sourcing for the authority envelope and priors, open questions. Not sent to the model.

allOf.$comment: Every other seat has no hidden type.
psyche is Red-only (northern_fleet, kremlin) and required there.
Non-Red seats must not carry a psyche.

seat.description: The 9 LLM personas, in the order given in contracts/seats.md. nsc is the human-playable seat; in a headless run it is filled by an LLM persona or by the auto-approval rule in env_config_schema.json#/properties/release_policy.

rule_actor.description: The 6 scripted rule actors in contracts/seats.md. They emit events and receive messages but never take menu actions and never have a spec. hacktivist_injects carries a per-run hidden affiliation (russian_directed | freelance | opportunistic) that is ground truth, not a spec field.

actor.description: Anything that can originate or receive traffic: the 9 seats, the 6 rule actors, plus 'environment' for the physical world and 'system' for engine bookkeeping.
